#

:::{.columns .tiny}

::::{.column width="40%" .fragment}
:::::{.box style="height: 275px"}
When an effect depends counterfactually on a cause, in general it will depend on much else as well. If the cause had occurred but other circumstances had been different, the effect would not have occurred. To the extent this is so, the dependence is sensitive.

<br>

[Lewis (1986)]{style="float: right"}

:::::

![](https://philosophy.princeton.edu/sites/g/files/toruqf2381/files/styles/freeform_750w/public/featured/lewis.jpg){height=200 style="float: right"}
::::

::::{.column width="10%"}
::::

::::{.column width="40%"}
:::::{.box style="height: 275px"}
A causal claim is insensitive to the extent to which it would continue to hold under various sorts of changes in the actual circumstances. The sensitivity of counterfactuals is understood similarly.

<br><br><br>

[Woodward (2006)]{style="float: right"}

:::::

![](https://www.hps.pitt.edu/sites/default/files/styles/person_image/public/person-img/Woodward.jpg){height=200 style="float: right"}
::::

:::

# The central claim {.dark}

[The concept of counterfactual sensitivity bundles together two distinct components]{style="font-size: 1.25em;"}

<br>

:::{.smaller}
::::{.fragment}
[**Instrumental role:**]{.ucl-light-orange}
producing desired outcomes
::::

::::{.fragment}
[**Epistemic role:**]{.ucl-light-blue}
weighing uncertainty
::::
:::


## A quick sketch


[You’re an investor choosing between two companies:]{.fragment}

:::{.incremental .much-smaller}
 - Company A is expected to perform well and has a stable profile
 - Company B should perform equally well but has an unstable profile
:::

<br>

:::{.fragment}
[Instrumental standpoint:]{.ucl-light-orange} 

::::{.columns .much-smaller}
:::::{.column width="5%"}
:::::

:::::{.column width="95%"}
Each company generates the same expected profit, so it doesn't really matter which choice you make
:::::
::::

:::

:::{.fragment}
[Epistemic standpoint:]{.ucl-light-blue}

::::{.columns .much-smaller}
:::::{.column width="5%"}
:::::

:::::{.column width="95%"}
You should choose Company B since it's more predictable
:::::
::::
:::


# A formal definition of counterfactual sensitivity {.dark}

## Causal graphs

:::{.r-stack}
[$\mathcal{G} = \{ \mathcal{V}, \mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F}, P(\mathcal{U}) \}$]{.fragment fragment-index=1}
:::

:::{.columns}
::::{.column width="50%"}
:::::{.r-stack}
:::::{.fragment fragment-index=4 .much-smaller}
[$\mathcal{F}$]{.center-horizontally}
$$
\begin{align*}
    AP &:= U_{AP} \\
    NC &:= U_{NC} \\
    WP &:= AP \wedge NC
\end{align*}
$$
:::::
:::::

:::::{.fragment fragment-index=5 .much-smaller}
[$P(\mathcal{U})$]{.center-horizontally}
$$
\begin{align*}
    P(U_{AP}) &= .90 \\
    P(U_{NC}) &= .01
\end{align*}
$$
:::::
::::

::::{.column width="50%"}
:::::{.r-stack}
::::::{.fragment fragment-index=2}

```{.tikz width=500}
    \node[state] (AP) [left=.5cm of WP, yshift=.66cm] { $AP$ };
    \node[state] (NC) [left=.5cm of WP, yshift=-.66cm] { $NC$ };
    \node[state, unboxed, hidden] (UAP) [left=.5cm of AP] { $U_{AP}$ };
    \node[state, unboxed, hidden] (UNC) [left=.5cm of NC] { $U_{NC}$ };
    
    \node[unboxed, hidden] (U) [above=.1cm of UAP] { $\mathcal{U}$ };
    \node[unboxed] (V) [right=1.4cm of U] { $\mathcal{V}$ };
    
    \path (AP) edge (WP);
    \path (NC) edge (WP);
    \path[hidden] (UAP) edge (AP);
    \path[hidden] (UNC) edge (NC);
\end{tikzpicture}
```

## Counterfactual sensitivity

:::{.center-vertically .left }
::::{.box .ucl-white-bg .ucl-dark-purple-outline style="padding: 0px" .fragment fragment-index=1}
:::::{.fragment fragment-index=4}
[$\mathfrak{N}(\mathcal{U})$]{.absolute top=15 left=15 .ucl-mid-purple style="font-size: 1.25em"}

<br>

```{r}
#| label: mvnorm_1
#| fig-width: 3.66
#| fig-height: 2.5
mu <- c(0, 0)
sigma <- c(1, 1)
rho <- .5
omega <- matrix(c(1, rho, rho, 1), nrow=2)

D <- dist_multivariate_normal(mu=list(mu),
                              sigma=list(diag(sigma) %*% omega %*% diag(sigma)))

d <- expand_grid(x=seq(-4, 4, by=.05),
                 y=seq(-4, 4, by=.05)) |>
  mutate(z=map2_dbl(x, y, ~ density(D, at=c(.x, .y))[[1]]))


ggplot(d, aes(x=x, y=y, alpha=z)) +
  geom_raster(fill=ucl_mid_purple) +
  scale_alpha_continuous(range=c(0, 1)) +
  coord_fixed(xlim=c(-3, 3), ylim=c(-3, 3)) +
  theme_void(paper=NA) +
  theme(legend.position='none')
```
:::::

[$u$]{.center-xy .much-larger}
::::
:::

:::{.fragment fragment-index=2}
[$Y_{X=x'}$]{.absolute left=400 top=250}

[$\Longrightarrow$]{.center-vertically style="font-size: 2.5em; left: 375px"}
:::

:::{.center-vertically .right}

[$Y_{X=x'}(u')$]{.ucl-mid-purple .tiny .absolute top="25%" left="66%" .fragment fragment-index=5}

## Counterfactual sensitivity

:::{.larger .center-xy}
$$
\begin{align*}
&\textrm{Sensitivity}_{\mathfrak{N},\delta,f}\left(Y_{X=x'}(u) = y'\right) \\
&\quad\equiv f\left( \mathbb{E}_{u' \sim \mathfrak{N}(\mathcal{U})} \left[ \delta \left( Y_{X=x'}(u'), y' \right)\right] \right)
\end{align*}
$$
:::

# Decomposing sensitivity {.dark}

## Decomposing sensitivity

:::{.absolute left=105 bottom=125 width=350 height=55 .ucl-light-blue-bg style="opacity: 50%;" .fragment fragment-index=6}
:::

:::{.absolute right=64 bottom=125 width=490 height=55 .ucl-light-orange-bg style="opacity: 50%;" .fragment fragment-index=6}
:::


:::{.much-smaller}
<br>

::::{.r-stack}
[$$\textrm{Sensitivity}_{\mathfrak{N},\delta,f}(Y_{X=x'}(u)=y') \equiv f\left( \mathbb{E}_{u' \sim \mathfrak{N}(\mathcal{U})} \left[ \delta \left( Y_{X=x'}(u'), y' \right)\right] \right)$$]{.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=1}

::::{.fragment fragment-index=1}
$$\textrm{Sensitivity}_{\mathfrak{N}}(Y_{X=x'}(u)=y') \equiv \,\sqrt{\mathbb{E}_{u'\sim\mathfrak{N}(\mathcal{U})}\left[(Y_{X=x'}(u') - y')^2\right]}$$
:::::
::::


[$\quad= \sqrt{\textrm{Var}_{u'\sim\mathfrak{N}(\mathcal{U})}\left[Y_{X=x'}(u') - y'\right] + \mathbb{E}_{u'\sim\mathfrak{N}(\mathcal{U})}\left[Y_{X=x'}(u') - y'\right]^2}$]{.fragment fragment-index=2}

[$\quad= \sqrt{\textrm{Var}_{u'\sim\mathfrak{N}(\mathcal{U})}\left[Y_{X=x'}(u')\right] + \left(\mathbb{E}_{u'\sim\mathfrak{N}(\mathcal{U})}\left[Y_{X=x'}(u')\right] - y'\right)^2}$]{.fragment fragment-index=3}

[$\quad= \sqrt{\textrm{Var}_{\mathfrak{N}}\left[Y_{X=x'}\right] + \textrm{Bias}\left(\mathbb{E}_{\mathfrak{N}}\left[Y_{X=x'}\right], \; y'\right)^2}$]{.fragment fragment-index=4}

[$\quad= \sqrt{\textrm{Var}_{\mathfrak{N}}\left[Y \;\vert\; do(X=x')\right] + \textrm{Bias}\left(\mathbb{E}_{\mathfrak{N}}\left[Y \;\vert\; do(X=x')\right], \; y'\right)^2}$]{.fragment fragment-index=5}
:::


## Special case for binary variables

:::{.much-smaller}
<br>

::::{.r-stack}
$$
\begin{align*}
\textrm{Sensitivity}_{\mathfrak{N}}(Y_{X=x'}(u)=y') &\equiv \,\sqrt{\mathbb{E}_{u'\sim\mathfrak{N}(\mathcal{U})}\left[(Y_{X=x'}(u') - y')^2\right]} \\
&= \sqrt{\mathfrak{N}(Y\ne y'\;\vert\; do(X=x'))}
\end{align*}
$$
::::
:::

:::{.ucl-white-bg .absolute right=60 top=240 width=500 height=75 .fragment .fade-out}
:::


## Example: robust sufficiency


:::{.columns }
::::{.column width="60%" .much-smaller}

[$\textrm{Sensitivity}_{\mathfrak{N}}(WP_{AP=1}(u)=1)$]{.fragment}

[$\quad= \sqrt{\mathfrak{N}(WP = 0 \;\vert\; do(AP=1))}$]{.fragment}

[$\quad= \sqrt{\mathfrak{N}(WP = 0 \;\vert\; AP=1)}$]{.fragment}

[$\quad= \sqrt{\mathfrak{N}(NC = 0)}$]{.fragment}

[$\quad\approx 0.99$]{.fragment}

<br>

:::::{.fragment}
$\textrm{Sensitivity}_{\mathfrak{N}}(WP_{NC=1}(u)=1)$

$\quad= \sqrt{\mathfrak{N}(AP = 0)}$

$\quad\approx 0.32$
:::::

::::

::::{.column width="40%"}

## [Counterfactual bias and variance]{ .much-smaller }

:::{.r-stack}
::::{.fragment}
```{r}
#| label: bias_variance_1
bias_variance_plot <- function(
  bias, variance, y_prime=0, show_bias=TRUE, show_variance=TRUE, nudge=.15
) {  
  p <- ggplot(tibble(Bias=bias, Variance=variance)) +
    stat_slab(aes(xdist=dist_normal(Bias, sqrt(Variance))), fill="grey90") +
    geom_vline(aes(xintercept=y_prime), linetype='dotted') +
    geom_text(aes(x=x, y=y), label=expression(Y["X=x'"]*"(u)"), size=4, hjust=1,
      data=tibble(x=y_prime-2*nudge, y=.95)) +
    scale_x_continuous(expression(Y["X=x'"])) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand=expansion(mult=c(0, .1))) +
    theme_classic(18, paper=NA) +
    theme(
      axis.title.y=element_blank(),
      axis.text=element_blank(),
      axis.ticks=element_blank(),
      axis.line.y=element_blank(),
      axis.line.x=element_blank(),
      strip.text.x=element_text(color=ucl_light_blue, face='bold'),
      strip.text.y=element_text(color=ucl_light_orange, face='bold'),
      axis.line.x.bottom=element_line(linewidth=1)
    )

  if (show_bias) {
    p <- p + geom_segment(
      aes(x=y_prime-nudge, xend=Bias+nudge), y=.5, linewidth=1.5, color=ucl_light_orange
    )
  }
  if (show_variance) {
    p <- p + geom_segment(
      aes(x=Bias-sqrt(Variance), xend=Bias+sqrt(Variance)),
      y=.1, linewidth=1.5, color=ucl_light_blue
    )
  }

  p
}

p1 <- bias_variance_plot(0, 1)  + facet_grid(~ Variance, labeller=label_both)
p2 <- bias_variance_plot(0, 10) + facet_grid(Bias ~ Variance, labeller=label_both)
p3 <- bias_variance_plot(3, 1)
p4 <- bias_variance_plot(3, 10) + facet_grid(Bias ~ ., labeller=label_both)

((p1 + hide_plot(p2) +
  hide_plot(p3) + hide_plot(p4)) &
  coord_cartesian(xlim=c(-6, 8))) +
  plot_layout(guides='collect')
```

# The central claim {.dark}

[The concept of counterfactual sensitivity bundles together two distinct components]{style="font-size: 1.25em;"}

<br>

:::{.smaller}
[**Instrumental role:**]{.ucl-light-orange}
producing desired outcomes

[$$\left(\mathbb{E}_{\mathfrak{N}}\left[Y \;\vert\; do(X=x')\right] - y'\right)^2$$]{.fragment .ucl-light-orange}

[**Epistemic role:**]{.ucl-light-blue}
weighing uncertainty

[$$\textrm{Var}_{\mathfrak{N}}\left[Y \;\vert\; do(X=x')\right]$$]{.fragment .ucl-light-blue}
:::


## Returning to our example
You’re an investor choosing between two companies:

:::{.much-smaller}
 - Company A is expected to perform well and has a stable profile
 - Company B should perform equally well but has an unstable profile
:::

<br>

\DeclareMathOperator*{\argmax}{argmax}
\DeclareMathOperator*{\argmin}{argmin}


:::{.fragment}
[Instrumental standpoint:]{.ucl-light-orange} 

::::{.columns .much-smaller}
:::::{.column width="5%"}
:::::

:::::{.column width="95%"}
Under the policy [$\argmax_{x \in \{A, B\}} \mathbb{E}_\mathfrak{N}\left[Y \;\vert\; do(X=x)\right]$]{.much-smaller .ucl-light-orange}, it doesn't matter which company you choose!
:::::
::::

:::

:::{.fragment}
[Epistemic standpoint:]{.ucl-light-blue}

::::{.columns .much-smaller}
:::::{.column width="5%"}
:::::

:::::{.column width="95%"}
Under the policy [$\argmin_{x \in \{A, B\}} \textrm{Var}_\mathfrak{N}\left[Y \;\vert\; do(X=x)\right]$]{.much-smaller .ucl-light-blue}, you should choose Company A *because it gives you more control*!
:::::
::::
:::


## Conclusions
:::{.center-vertically}
:::{.fragment}
We can think of sensitivity as distance between:

::::{.much-smaller}
   - The counterfactual outcome
   - The interventional distribution with respect to $\mathfrak{N}$
::::
:::


[This explains:]{.fragment}

:::{.incremental .much-smaller}
  - why causal judgments are sensitive to norms
  - why "counterfactual" models are often interventional
  - how confidence relates to causal judgments
  - how sensitivity also guides future-oriented decisions
:::
:::
